correctness.rationale: For any nonnegative mass on a finite-field line pencil, scalar dilation averaging preserves the origin mass and does not increase the maximum nonzero Fourier modulus. Exact finite-field character sums yield one frequency level t=a-B off all selected annihilator lines and one level t+q b_j on each chosen dual line. Averaging line weights (fixed sum B) cannot increase the maximum. For the resulting two-level mass, positivity gives t in [-1/(q-1),1], and the explicit strictly one-dimensional minimax max(|t|,(1+(k-1)t)/k) has a unique optimizer at t=-1/(2k-1) if q<=2k and t=-1/(q-1) otherwise. The optimizer is attained; uniqueness after center-mass-preserving averaging proves the origin atom of every optimizer is rigid. The q=k, characteristic-two and boundary q=2k cases are included; full pencil k=q+1 is excluded. The embedded Python checker passes 4,376 direct nonzero Fourier comparisons over field orders 2,3,4,5,7,8,9,11, including nonprime fields. Finite checks supplement but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: Finite-field Kakeya and partial-direction covers naturally ask how Fourier-flat a probability measure can be. The exact all-prime-power, all-direction, all-2<=k<=q minimax value improves a general incidence bound and locates a sharp phase threshold: below or at q=2k the canonical measure is spectrally equimodular on all nonzero frequencies, while above it optimizers omit the common intersection. The center atom is forced for every optimizer, not just symmetric examples, and uniform mass is optimum only at q=2k-2. These are structural and quantitatively sharp features of a motivated natural invariant, not a fixed small computation or a tautological normalizing check.
